description: Issue #883: a cross-vendor review of b3dbae4b3 (#841/#862) found seven EtlSchedulerService IgnoreQueryFilters() call sites reachable from HTTP controllers (_EtlJobController/_EtlRunLogController/EtlJobDefinitionVM) with no check that the caller-supplied jobId belonged to the caller's own tenant -- an IDOR letting tenant A's ETLAdmin read (DryRun's source-data preview rows) or operate on (TriggerNow/Reschedule/Pause/Resume/Abort/Enable/Disable) tenant B's job. Fixed via LoadJobDefinitionForCallerAsync, a shared private helper every affected method now funnels through: it applies a TenantCode == callerTenantCode predicate unless the caller explicitly passes declaredSystemQuery: true (the #843 contract, reused verbatim). This mutant neutralizes exactly that guard (`if (!declaredSystemQuery)` -> `if (false)`), so the tenant predicate is never applied and the helper reverts to pre-#883 behaviour -- unconditional IgnoreQueryFilters() with no ownership check -- for every method that routes through it (TriggerNowAsync, RescheduleAsync, DryRunAsync, and, via EnsureCallerOwnsJobAsync, PauseAsync/ResumeAsync/AbortAsync/DisableAsync). Checked against five of #883's HTTP-reachable cross-tenant negative controls that route through this specific helper -- TriggerNow_CrossTenantJobId_Rejected, DryRun_CrossTenantJobId_Rejected, Pause_CrossTenantJobId_Rejected, Resume_CrossTenantJobId_Rejected, Reschedule_CrossTenantJobId_Rejected -- each of which seeds a job under tenant B, authenticates as tenant A's ETLAdmin, and asserts the cross-tenant call is rejected (404/400, matching the pre-fix 'not found' shape for a genuinely nonexistent id); with the mutant applied, every one of those calls instead succeeds against tenant B's job (TriggerNow schedules and returns 200; Pause/Resume proceed to a real Quartz no-op-then-unconditional-DB-write and return 200; DryRun proceeds past the id check into real schema-introspection logic and no longer returns the 404 'not found' shape; Reschedule's own DB-level assertion -- CronExpression must be unchanged -- catches the write even if Quartz's own trigger-not-found response happens to reuse the same HTTP status). Abort_CrossTenantJobId_Rejected is deliberately EXCLUDED from this mutant's red_tests: verified empirically that it stays green under this exact mutation, because AbortAsync's own business logic (Interrupt() returning false for a job that legitimately isn't running in Quartz, since this test's seeded job is never actually executing) produces the SAME 400 Bad Request as the tenant-ownership rejection, and IsQuickDebug=false masks the distinguishing exception message into an identical generic string either way -- it is not a reliable kill signal for this specific line, though the test itself remains a valid functional regression check (tenant A still cannot abort tenant B's job, for whichever reason). SkipNext and RerunFromSnapshotAsync's own runLog lookup are NOT in this mutant's red_tests either -- they carry their own independent `if (!declaredSystemQuery)` guards (EtlSchedulerService.cs, inline rather than routed through this shared helper) and are covered by their own existing/updated mutants instead. The green control, SkipNext_OwnTenantJobId_Succeeds, is unaffected by this specific line (SkipNext never calls LoadJobDefinitionForCallerAsync) and proves the mutation's build/test environment itself is not broken.
target_symbol: EtlSchedulerService.LoadJobDefinitionForCallerAsync -- the `if (!declaredSystemQuery)` guard before the TenantCode predicate is applied
